diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\matM \in \CC^{n \xx n}$ be a nonzero multiple of a unitary matrix

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bridges the two transforms by equating the original-domain relative error with the discarded fraction of the M1-transform-domain energy: $1-\beta_{r_\gamma(\matM_1)} = \FNormS{\tX-\tX_{\bs{r}^{(1)}}}/\FNormS{\tX}$. The invoked identity (the multirank-truncation error equals the sum of discarded transform-domain singular values, \cite[Thm 3.8]{KilmerPNAS}) is established only for $\matM$ a nonzero multiple of a unitary matrix; for $\matM_1=\matD\matQ$ with non-uniform $\matD$ the original-domain Frobenius norm weights slice $k$ by $\mu_k^{-2}$, so discarding a component of scaled energy $\alpha=\mu_k^2\nu$ costs $\nu=\alpha/\mu_k^2$, not $\alpha$, and the equality is false. Counterexample within all hypotheses: $n=3$, $\matM_0=\matI_3$, $\matM_1=\diag(2,1,1)$ (rows real, so \Cref{lem:conditions_real_tubal_ring} holds and \Cref{thm:necessary_sufficient_conditions_optimality} applies with $\matD=\diag(2,1,1)$, $\matQ=\matI$), and the real tube $\tX=(\sqrt{50},\sqrt{49.4},\sqrt{48.6})$. For $\gamma=0.6$: under $\matM_0$ the sorted energies $(50,49.4,48.6)$ give $\omega_1=0.338<0.6\le\omega_2=0.671$, so $r_\gamma(\matM_0)=2$; under $\matM_1$ they are $(200,49.4,48.6)$ with total $298$, so $\beta_1=0.671\ge0.6$ and $r_\gamma(\matM_1)=1$. Hence $r_\gamma(\matM_0)=2>1=r_\gamma(\matM_1)$, contradicting the theorem.

issues.why_classification: The statement is refuted by an explicit example satisfying every stated hypothesis; any complete resolution abandons the compared quantity (energy measured in each transform's own domain) or excludes the non-uniformly scaled regime the theorem was written for, so no comparable version of the stated guarantee survives.

We have $\bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \tU_{:,j} = \sum_{k=1}^{r'} \bs{z}_{j,k} \mm \vec{\mat{W}}_k$ for some $\bs{z}_{j,k} \in \FFF_n$ and all $j \in [r]$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives only that for each generator index $j$ some index $k(j)$ has $\bs{s}_{j,j}\mm\vec{\matW}_{k(j)}^\CT\mm\tU_{:,j}\ne\bs{0}$, and concludes $r'\ge r$. This is a non sequitur: distinct $j$ may be witnessed by the same $k$, and over a tubal ring (which has zero divisors) nothing forces the witnesses to be distinct, so no lower bound on $r'$ follows. The irredundancy half of the lemma is therefore unproven as written. It is locally repairable: for fixed $j_0$, the $\RR_n$-linear functional $\vec{\matW}\mapsto(\bs{s}_{j_0,j_0}\mm\tU_{:,j_0})^\CT\mm\vec{\matW}$ vanishes on every other generator (slice-wise orthonormality of $\wh{\tU}$) while sending $\bs{s}_{j_0,j_0}\mm\tU_{:,j_0}$ to $\bs{s}_{j_0,j_0}^\CT\mm\bs{s}_{j_0,j_0}\ne\bs{0}$; hence no generator lies in the span of the others.

establishing Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncation.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement claims optimality for both multi-rank and t-rank truncations, but the proof only treats a target multi-rank: it maps $\tX_{\bs{r}}$ to a tubal-length, invokes tubal-length optimality, and concludes 'establishing Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncation'; the t-rank feasible set $\{\tY:\trnk{\matM}\tY\le r\}$ is never considered. The missing step is short but absent: the t-rank-$r$ truncation equals the multirank-$(r,\ldots,r)$ truncation (the tube ordering is coordinatewise, so slice-wise truncation at depth $r$ agrees with keeping the first $r$ tubes), and every tensor of t-rank $\le r$ has multirank $\le(r,\ldots,r)$, so the proven multirank case yields the t-rank case.

failure_location.quote: Then, $\RR_n$ also satisfies Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncations and t-rank truncations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Append the short argument above (t-rank-$r$ truncation = multirank-$(r,\ldots,r)$ truncation, and the feasible-set inclusion) to the proof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we provide a complete characterization of the family of tubal products that yield an Eckart-Young type result.
In what follows, we provide a complete characterization of those choices of transforms $\matM$ that yield Eckart-Young type optimality results for t-rank and multirank truncations of the tSVDM.
establishing Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncation.

Importantly, \Cref{thm:lengthopt_implies_multirankopt} tells us that in order to establish necessary and sufficient conditions on $\matM$ for Eckart-Young optimality with respect to multi-rank and t-rank truncations, it suffices to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for Eckart-Young optimality with respect to tubal-length truncations.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose (title, abstract, \Cref{q:q1} discussion, Section openings) promises a complete -- necessary and sufficient -- characterization of the transforms yielding Eckart-Young optimality 'for t-rank and multirank truncations'. The source establishes: (i) sufficiency, \matM=\matD\matQ implies optimality for tubal-length, multirank and (modulo the gap in \Cref{thm:lengthopt_implies_multirankopt}) t-rank truncations; (ii) necessity, but only under the hypothesis of Eckart-Young optimality for tubal-length truncation (\Cref{lem:nec.opt.disjoint.idempotent,lem:nec.opt.intra.idempotent.ortho} both assume the tubal-length property of \Cref{def:optimality.prop}), and the only bridge to the other notions, \Cref{thm:lengthopt_implies_multirankopt}, is one-directional (length optimality implies the others). No argument anywhere shows that multirank-optimality, let alone t-rank optimality (the notion of \Cref{eq:eckart_young.trank} on which the abstract's 'best low-rank approximation ... by truncating its tubal SVD' is based), implies tubal-length optimality or the DQ form. Hence the claimed necessity half of the characterization is established only for the newly defined tubal-length notion (and, by a short unprovided argument, for multirank), not for t-rank.

failure_location.quote: we now turn to the main result of this work, that is, a complete characterization of the transformation matrices $\matM$ for inducing tubal rings that satisfy Eckart-Young type optimality properties for tubal-length truncation (therefore also for t-rank and multi-rank truncations).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the prose to the proven scope (characterization for tubal-length truncation, transferred to multirank), add the short argument that multirank optimality for all valid multiranks is equivalent to tubal-length optimality (the two feasible sets coincide by \Cref{lem:principal_length_and_multirank,lem:length_and_multirank_order_preserving}), and either prove or drop the necessity claim for t-rank.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised necessary-and-sufficient characterization of tubal products for Eckart-Young optimality exceeds what is proven: for t-rank optimality the necessity half is unsupported, so the 'complete characterization' guarantee at the level of the title/abstract/intro is broader than the formal content.
issues.title: Headline 'complete characterization' overclaims: necessity for t-rank (and multirank) optimality is not established
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening plus a contained equivalence argument; the main formal characterization (tubal-length, and multirank via the short argument) and all its applications survive, so there is no major loss and no new global proof architecture.
